title: Basis-anchor decay: stale open issues re-verify their own grounding or close themselves
idea: The intake brief's own first pre-mortem is backlog rot — this very ideation process will generate faster than the fleet executes, and wave-tagging only orders the rot, it does not drain it. Since every issue in this backlog carries a basis with concrete anchors (file:line, decision anchors, quoted evidence), make that basis a liveness contract: a periodic cheap-tier pass re-verifies the anchors of issues untouched for N days against current code and journal state. Anchors that moved or evidence that has since been fixed produce an automated 'basis decayed' comment and a close-as-stale proposal at the next board review; anchors that hold re-stamp the issue as still grounded. The backlog becomes self-pruning by the same provenance discipline that created it.
basis: Intake brief 'Pre-mortems recorded' item 1: 'Backlog rot — generation outpaces execution bandwidth; the fleet churns under open issues. Mitigation: wave tagging, wave-1 bandwidth multipliers' — the recorded mitigation orders execution but contains no pruning mechanism, which is the gap this fills. Reinforced by grounding brief §6 item 2 (provenance/status claims must be re-verified against current state, 4 learnings).
outcome_shape: Merged: basis-anchor re-verification script + scheduled mission-control pass that comments/labels decayed issues and surfaces close proposals at board review.
dod_sketch: Merged: basis-anchor re-verification script + scheduled mission-control pass; verified when a seeded issue with a moved/fixed anchor emits a 'basis decayed' comment + close proposal while an issue with holding anchors is re-stamped green.

title: Revisit-when conditions become checkable predicates: decisions re-open on evidence, not memory
idea: The binding-decision register is the backbone of this whole ideation process, and every row carries a revisit-when clause — yet nothing anywhere evaluates those clauses; they are prose dead letters that depend on someone remembering them at the right moment. That is the same disease as the journal's stale-claim learnings (provenance must be re-verified against current state). Make revisit-when machinery: DECISIONS.md entries carry an optional machine-checkable predicate (a grep, a file-exists, a version threshold, a registry lookup), and a /retro-time (or CI) sweep evaluates them and flags decisions whose revisit condition has come true — e.g. {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} auto-flags the day a read-only-sandbox profile ships, and {#worker-cache-scheduling} flags when idle-poll telemetry crosses its stated threshold. First-principles argument: a constraint whose release condition is unmonitored converges to a permanent constraint, so the fleet silently ossifies around decisions whose premises have expired; cheap predicate evaluation is strictly better than relying on human recall across dozens of decisions and months of drift.
basis: Argument: (1) the grounding brief's own rule — 'ideas contradicting one must engage its revisit-when' (section 2 header) — makes revisit-when clauses load-bearing gates for all future work; (2) every listed clause ('read-only-sandbox profile ships', 'named-teammate residency proves insufficient', 'idle-poll justifies a formal wave queue') is a testable world-state, yet no process, CI job, or skill step evaluates any of them; (3) the journal independently records 4 learnings that unverified stale claims persist until lucky operator recall (grounding section 6.2) — the identical failure mode. Therefore unmonitored revisit conditions guarantee either ossification (constraint outlives its premise) or accidental violation (someone forgets the constraint exists); a predicate sweep eliminates both at near-zero cost.
outcome_shape: Merged PR: DECISIONS.md entry schema gains an optional revisit-check field + a sweep script wired into /retro (and optionally CI) that evaluates predicates and emits a came-true report, with existing register entries backfilled where checkable.
dod_sketch: Merged PR: DECISIONS.md schema gains a revisit-check predicate field + /retro-wired sweep script; verified when a backfilled entry whose world-state is now true emits a 'came-true' report and a still-false one stays silent. (Corrected moonshot→structural: bounded schema + sweep, not open-ended research.)

title: One append-only ledger substrate under the pool's 45 ledgers and 19 receipts
idea: The pool proposes ~45 ledger ideas and ~19 receipt ideas — cost ledger (T2-F4-6), cache-economics ledger (T4-F3-5), consensus replay log (T5-F5-8), delegation chain-of-custody (T15-F2-8), tier-regret ledger (T12-F4-7), reclamation ledger (T6-F4-1), evidence custody chain (T7-F5-6), dispatch-casualty manifest (H-F1-2). Every one independently re-solves the same four problems: append-only storage, content addressing/tamper evidence, where the file lives relative to worktree blast radius (T15-F3-8), and how /retro queries it. Nobody wrote the substrate: a single fleet ledger primitive — one JSONL append-only, hash-chained, worktree-external store with a typed 'kind' column and a tiny reader API — that every per-theme ledger becomes a row-kind of, not a bespoke file format. Without this, convergence ships a dozen incompatible ledgers and the {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7} sprawl concern reproduces itself at the artifact layer.
basis: Gap in pool: jq census over pool.json — 45 titles matching 'ledger', 19 matching 'receipt', zero ideas proposing a shared substrate they instantiate. Binding decision {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7} (grounding brief §2) puts a consolidation burden of proof on new machinery; shipping 10+ bespoke ledger formats is the exact sprawl it names. The /outcome campaign decision already fixes one design point ('cost ledger = leaf-produced fact'), which the substrate must honor: leaves append, coordinators read.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/fleet_ledger.py (append/verify/query, hash-chained JSONL, worktree-external path resolution) + a references/ledger-kinds.md registry; two existing ledger consumers (cost ledger, verify evidence) migrated as proof; conformance test that a later PASS row cannot mutate an earlier FAIL row.
dod_sketch: Merged PR: fleet_ledger.py (hash-chained JSONL append/verify/query) + ledger-kinds.md registry + two migrated consumers; verified by a conformance test proving a later PASS row cannot mutate/overwrite an earlier FAIL row.

title: Name the import mechanism: where cross-plugin shared primitives actually live and how a plugin gets them
idea: At least 28 pool ideas say 'shared primitive every plugin/fan-out site imports' (tier palette T3-F4-1, concurrency resolver T13-F4-1, consensus kernel T5-F6-1, liveness engine T6-F4-3, reclaim primitive T6-F4-1, delegation receipt T15-F4-1, posture primitive T4-F4-1). None answers the load-bearing question: plugins are independently installed marketplace artifacts with no shared Python package path — cross-plugin import is not currently a thing. H-F6-8 circles it for contracts ('the marketplace is the contract bus') but stops short of code. The missing idea: decide and build the fleet-commons distribution mechanism — either (a) a fleet-core plugin whose scripts/ is the canonical home, with sibling plugins resolving it via marketplace-installed path discovery plus a vendored-fallback shim, or (b) a real Python package published from this repo that CLI plugins declare as a dependency. Without this decision, all 28 'shared primitive' survivors silently degrade into copy-paste mirrors — recreating exactly the T14 contract-drift disease the pool is trying to cure.
basis: First-principles: grounding brief §1 lists 8 independently versioned plugins; the marketplace installs each in isolation, so 'X.py every plugin imports' has no resolvable import path today — verified by the repo layout (each plugin's scripts live under its own skills/ tree, tests import via repo-root paths that do not exist at install time). 28 pool ideas (jq census on 'shared primitive'/'imports') depend on this unnamed mechanism; if unresolved, each ships as a hand-copy, which the 4-repo contract-mirror-drift evidence (grounding §3 finding 1) shows will drift. Engages {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7}: a fleet-core home is consolidation, not sprawl — it deletes future copies rather than adding a surface.
outcome_shape: A DECISIONS.md entry choosing the distribution mechanism (with rejected alternative recorded) plus the first PR implementing it: fleet-core resolution shim + one real consumer (tier palette or concurrency resolver) imported through it from two different plugins, with an install-time integration test proving resolution works outside the repo checkout.
dod_sketch: Merged: DECISIONS.md distribution-mechanism entry (rejected alt recorded) + resolution shim + one primitive imported through it from two plugins; verified by an install-time integration test proving cross-plugin resolution works outside the repo checkout.

title: The dark half of the fleet: an explicit in-or-out verdict and primitive-parity pass for deploy, home-lab-ops, unifi, and redis-channel
idea: The grounding brief maps 8 plugins; the 15 themes and ~771 ideas concentrate almost entirely on saga, team-execution, mission-control, and agy. jq census: 7 ideas mention unifi/home-lab-ops, 8 mention redis-channel/discord — under 2% of the pool for half the fleet. A 'turn the fleet spectacular' backlog that silently ignores four plugins either believes they are fine (unverified) or out of scope (undeclared). The missing meta-move: a deliberate per-plugin verdict pass — for each dark plugin, decide (a) it adopts the wave-1 fleet primitives where its shape matches (deploy gains ledger/receipt evidence and ship-ceremony integration per T7-F2-8's baton; redis-channel becomes the gate transport of G-negative-space-6; home-lab-ops portal gates adopt the consent-receipt contract), or (b) it is declared lifecycle-peripheral in DECISIONS.md with a revisit-when — engaging {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7} honestly instead of by omission. Either verdict is fine; the absence of a verdict is the defect.
basis: Direct: grounding brief §1 fleet map lists 8 plugins (deploy 0.1.2, home-lab-ops 1.2.0, redis-channel 0.5.0, unifi 1.1.0 among them) while the §8 theme roster derives every theme from saga/team-execution/mission-control/agy evidence; pool census confirms <2% idea coverage of the other four. Binding decision {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7} makes sprawl an active concern that cuts both ways — plugins kept in the portfolio should either participate in fleet primitives or have their peripheral status recorded; today neither is true, which is the same undeclared-scope disease the pool's own contract-census ideas (T14-F4-7: 'every contract must declare a guard') attack at the contract layer.
outcome_shape: A DECISIONS.md entry per dark plugin (participate-with-listed-primitives or peripheral-with-revisit-when) produced by one read-only survey pass, plus follow-on issues only for the 'participate' verdicts; the decision entries are the merged artifact, wave-tagged behind the primitives they depend on.
dod_sketch: Merged: one DECISIONS.md verdict entry per dark plugin (deploy/home-lab-ops/unifi/redis-channel) from a read-only survey pass, each stating participate-with-listed-primitives or peripheral-with-revisit-when; verified by all four plugins having an explicit non-empty verdict entry.
